title: Tax, Totals and the UBL Document
subtitle: Making the arithmetic LHDN receives add up, line by line, to the sen
outcomes: Describe the shape of a UBL 2.1 JSON invoice and the elements LHDN reads
Read a preview payload and verify header totals against line amounts
Explain how the app resolves tax type and rate for each line
Handle discounts, allowances and rounding differences without breaking reconciliation
Use the document hash to reason about idempotency and change detection

slides.title: What the app actually sends
bullets: UBL 2.1 expressed as JSON, with every scalar wrapped as {"_": value} as the mapping requires
InvoiceTypeCode carries listVersionID 1.1, tax scheme id OTH and classification list id CLASS
The envelope identifies supplier, customer, lines, tax totals and legal monetary totals
Serialisation is deterministic, so an unchanged invoice always produces the same bytes
That determinism is what makes a hash a reliable identity for a document
slides.notes: If the audience is technical, show a real payload from the preview dialog. The {"_": …} wrapping is the single most confusing part of UBL JSON, and seeing it once is better than describing it five times. The important business point is determinism: same data, same bytes, same hash, which underpins duplicate prevention.

slides.title: The header fields, and what each one decides
bullets: ID is the Sales Invoice name, so your naming series becomes LHDN's document number
IssueDate comes from the posting date; IssueTime is converted to UTC with a trailing Z
DocumentCurrencyCode must be MYR, since no other currency is accepted
InvoiceTypeCode decides invoice, credit, debit or refund, and drives the reference requirement
LegalMonetaryTotal carries line extension, tax total and the payable amount

rows: Must be unique at LHDN forever
May differ from grand total by rounding

slides.notes: Naming series is a compliance decision because the invoice number becomes a permanent LHDN identifier. If your series reuses numbers across sites or after a test environment reset, you will hit duplicate rejections. The other trap is the UTC timestamp: a late-night invoice can appear on the previous UTC day, which is fine, but a confused accountant will file a ticket about it.

slides.title: Inside an invoice line
bullets: InvoicedQuantity carries the quantity and a unitCode, with trailing zeros removed
LineExtensionAmount is the net amount after line discount, matching ERPNext's net amount
PriceAmount is the unit rate, and AllowanceCharge appears when the line was discounted
Item carries the description and the CommodityClassification with the MSIC code
Each line repeats its own tax treatment, which is what makes mixed-rate invoices possible
slides.notes: Line-level tax repetition surprises people who expect one tax block per invoice. It exists so that a single invoice can mix taxable and exempt supplies, which Malaysian businesses do constantly. The AllowanceCharge element is worth highlighting: a discount is expressed as a positive charge amount, not a negative price, and getting the sign wrong makes the arithmetic fail later.

slides.title: How the app decides each line's tax type and rate
bullets: First it reads the item tax rate snapshot that ERPNext wrote from the item tax template
Then it resolves invoice tax rows through the account-to-tax-type mapping
Then it falls back to the settings default, which is zero six with a zero rate
Tax types other than 01 to 05 are forced to a zero rate, so exemption cannot carry an amount
Per-line tax amounts are then reconciled against the invoice's total taxes and charges

callout.title: SST is not GST
callout.text: Malaysia has used SST since 2018. Nothing in this app relies on ERPNext's GST fields, and old GST tax templates should be retired before go-live.

slides.notes: This ordering is the heart of the app's tax logic. Reading the ERPNext snapshot first means the payload agrees with the ledger by construction. The reconciliation step is the safety net: if line tax does not add up to the invoice tax total, validation blocks the submission rather than sending arithmetic LHDN will reject. Mixed rates are normal, not exotic.

slides.title: Discounts, allowances and rounding
bullets: Line discounts become AllowanceCharge when quantity times rate exceeds the net amount
Negative prices are rejected by validation, so discounts must be modelled as discounts
Invoice-level rounding adjustments appear as a difference between grand total and payable amount
A difference above five sen is recorded as a warning on the log, and submission still proceeds
Never edit the payload by hand: fix the invoice so the document is reproducible
slides.notes: Rounding is where finance and compliance meet. LHDN wants totals that reconcile; ERPNext wants to round the grand total to the nearest sen. The app's five-sen tolerance and warning is a pragmatic compromise. Explain that the warning is a prompt to look, not an error, and that a pattern of warnings usually means the tax configuration needs attention.

slides.title: The hash is a fingerprint you can trust
bullets: The document hash is a SHA-256 of the serialised payload, computed before submission
Identical invoices produce identical hashes, which is how the app refuses to submit twice
The hash is stored on the log beside the exact bytes that were sent
Any change to a customer name, address or amount changes the hash, so change detection is trivial
Comparing a stored hash with a fresh preview is the fastest way to prove nothing drifted
slides.notes: Hashes sound cryptographic and intimidating, but the business use is simple: it is a tamper-evident receipt of what was sent. If an auditor asks whether the invoice changed after submission, recompute and compare. The same property powers idempotency, because a second submission attempt with the same hash is recognisably the same document.

slides.title: Using the preview as a review tool
bullets: Preview returns ok, errors, warnings, the document itself and the hash, without contacting LHDN
Errors block submission; warnings are recorded and the document still goes out
The preview dialog shows the UBL JSON so an accountant can read what will be sent
Preview is free and unlimited, so use it on every unusual invoice for the first month
A clean preview is the cheapest possible test of master data correctness
paths: Sales Invoice → Malaysia e-Invoice → Preview e-Invoice
Sales Invoice → Malaysia e-Invoice → Submit to MyInvois
Sales Invoice → Malaysia e-Invoice → e-Invoice Status
slides.notes: Encourage a habit rather than a rule: preview anything unfamiliar. The dialog is deliberately plain, because the audience is an accountant checking a customer name and a total, not a developer reading JSON. Point out that a clean preview with a stable hash is a strong signal that the document will be accepted.

slides.title: Proving the payload agrees with your ledger
bullets: Compare the payload's line extensions with the Sales Invoice net amounts, line by line
Compare the tax total with ERPNext's total taxes and charges, allowing only rounding
Compare the payable amount with the grand total and explain anything over five sen
Check the invoice type and billing reference on every note document
Keep the preview hash with the approval if a human signed off on a manual submission
slides.notes: This is the discipline that makes month-end possible. The payload is a second expression of the same transaction, so any divergence is a bug or a mapping problem. Doing it on a sample of invoices monthly catches configuration drift early. If a reviewer signs off a manual submission, the hash gives the sign-off something concrete to point at.

lab.title: Audit the arithmetic of a mixed-rate invoice
steps: Create a Sales Invoice with three lines: a 10 percent sales tax item, an 8 percent service tax item, and an exempt item
Add a line-level discount to the first line and an invoice-level rounding adjustment
Preview the document and expand the UBL JSON inside the dialog
Verify the InvoicedQuantity and unitCode for each line, and note how trailing zeros were dropped
Check that the discounted line carries an AllowanceCharge and that its sign is positive
Add the per-line tax amounts by hand and compare with the header TaxTotal
Change one quantity, preview again, and record how the hash changed
Restore the original quantity and confirm the hash returns to its first value
lab.done: You can predict the header tax total and the payable amount before previewing, you saw the discount expressed as an allowance, and the hash returned to its original value when the data did.

quiz.question: Which element tells LHDN whether a document is an invoice or a credit note?
quiz.why: InvoiceTypeCode carries 01 to 04, and types 02 to 04 also trigger the requirement for a billing reference to the original.

quiz.question: An invoice has a 20 sen rounding difference between ERPNext grand total and the payload payable amount. What happens?
options: A warning is recorded on the log and the submission still proceeds
The payable amount is silently adjusted
quiz.why: The app tolerates small rounding differences for the payable amount, records a warning, and lets the document go. Errors are reserved for arithmetic that does not reconcile.

quiz.question: Why does the app compute a hash before submitting?
options: To identify the document uniquely and prevent duplicate submissions
To sign the request with LHDN
quiz.why: The SHA-256 hash of the deterministic payload identifies the document, so a repeat attempt can be recognised rather than resubmitted.

quiz.question: A line has tax type E for exemption but carries a 5 percent rate. What does the app do?
options: Forces the rate to zero, because exemption cannot carry a tax amount
Rejects the invoice at LHDN and never locally
quiz.why: Only types 01 to 05 can carry a rate. Exemption and not-applicable codes are normalised to zero so the payload stays internally consistent.

quiz.question: You want to prove nothing changed since an invoice was submitted last month. What do you do?
options: Re-open the Sales Invoice and compare totals by eye
Preview now and compare the hash with the one stored on the log
Ask LHDN support for a copy
quiz.why: Deterministic serialisation means an unchanged document hashes identically. A hash match is proof the payload has not drifted.

narration: Chapter five is the payload, and the goal is simple: make the arithmetic LHDN receives add up to the sen. The document is UBL expressed as JSON, where every scalar is wrapped in an underscore key, and it is serialised deterministically, so the same invoice always produces the same bytes. That is why a hash can act as a fingerprint. The header carries the invoice number, the posting date, an issue time converted to UTC, the invoice type, the currency, and the legal monetary totals. The invoice number becomes a permanent LHDN identifier, so naming series is a compliance decision. Each line carries its quantity with a UN unit code, its net amount, its unit price, an allowance charge when discounted, and the MSIC classification. Tax appears twice: once per line and once in the header, which is what allows mixed rates on one invoice. Rates resolve from the ERPNext item tax snapshot first, then the tax account mapping, then the default, and anything outside tax types zero one to zero five is forced to zero. Line tax is then reconciled against the invoice tax total, so a mismatch is an error, not a surprise from LHDN. Discounts are allowances, never negative prices. A rounding gap over five sen on the payable amount is a warning, and the document still goes. Use the preview as a review tool: it is free, it never calls LHDN, and it shows errors, warnings, the JSON and the hash. In the lab you audit a mixed-rate invoice by hand.
